housing: Private renting is the largest tenure in Hammersmith and Fulham, at more than a third of households in 2021. Most of the stock is Victorian and Edwardian terraces, often split into flats, and red-brick mansion blocks, with large council estates in White City, Shepherd's Bush and West Kensington. Riverside developments in Sands End and Fulham Reach and new towers at White City have added many new-build apartments. Rents and prices are among the highest in outer west London, and many lets are flat-shares for young professionals.
checkinTips: Mansion blocks in Barons Court and West Kensington: photograph the communal entrance, lift and stairs, and record keys for the street door, the flat and any porter's fob.
Victorian terraces split into flats: photograph the shared hallway, meter cupboard and fire doors, and note who is responsible for the front garden and bins.
Loft and rear extensions in Fulham family houses: photograph rooflights, flat-roof areas visible from windows and any stains on ceilings below.
Riverside new-builds in Sands End and Fulham Reach: photograph balcony decking and drainage, underfloor heating controls and any marks on integrated appliances.
Original sash and bay windows: check cords, catches and seals and photograph any condensation or mould on sills and reveals.
tenantHelp: Private tenants can report disrepair, damp and mould to Hammersmith & Fulham Council's private sector housing team, which first asks the landlord to fix problems and can inspect and serve notices if they don't.
